title: Compact preflight hooks and lean dependency bootstrap for faster presubmit
author: Aisha Chen
description: Motivation: Presubmit run time and noisy CI resource consumption remain two of the top friction points for engineers. This change consolidates preflight hooks into a compact, stage-aware runner and introduces a two-stage dependency bootstrap so shallow PRs avoid installing heavy dev toolchains. Goals: reduce cold presubmit setup time, shrink presubmit image footprint, improve cache hit-rate for common paths, and expose lightweight lint telemetry for triage. Summary of changes: 1) Add .github/preflight.yml: declarative, stage-aware preflight definition that runs a small fastpath of checks first (format, small unit tests, lightweight lint plugin) and defers heavy checks (integration tests, full-typecheck, heavy linters) to a secondary stage when the fastpath passes. 2) Introduce ci/bootstrap.sh (two-stage): - stage A: install pinned runtime deps and workspace cache layers (fast, idempotent) - stage B: opt-in heavy toolchain install (deep-lint, compile toolchain) only executed for deep-checks or when explicitly requested. 3) Build a new docker/presubmit-slim.Dockerfile that splits layers so the frequent cacheable layers are near the top and heavy language toolchains live in a separate optional image to be pulled only for deep checks. 4) Add scripts/cache-warm.sh to proactively warm common dependency sets for CI runners and dev workstations. 5) Introduce a small lint plugin manifest and runtime shim (tools/lint-plugin/manifest.json) which emits structured telemetry for lint flakiness and cold-worker causes. 6) Update docs (docs/ci/presubmit.md) and Makefile targets to surface the opt-in behavior and fastpath toggles. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by infra and DX - [x] Unit tests for presubmit router logic - [x] Integration smoke for two-stage bootstrap on ephemeral runner - [x] Docs updated - [x] Rollout plan added Rollout plan: staged rollout using feature flag presubmit.fastpath in .github/feature-flags; start with 10% of PRs on main for 48h, expand to 50% if success metrics meet target. Monitoring: track presubmit setup time, presubmit total runtime, cache hit-rate, and number of deep-stage invocations. Expected improvement: ~35-45% reduction in median presubmit setup time on cold runners and ~40% smaller presubmit container download when fastpath only is used. Backout: revert the feature flag or revert merge; bootstrap.sh and preflight.yml are idempotent and will not block current workflows. Notes: This PR purposefully avoids changing lint rules or test gating semantics. The fastpath only reorders and scopes checks; heavy checks remain available and gated behind the second stage or explicit flags.

Tanya: asked for clarification on cache TTL and suggested 7d default (updated cache-warm.sh and docs). Liam: asked for a small benchmark showing end-to-end time reductions on a cold runner (added measurements to docs: median cold setup 78s -> 47s). CI initially failed on lint-plugin schema validation (fixed manifest and added unit test); reran checks and all green. Final approvals from Marco and Tanya after small followups; merged via squash. No outstanding unresolved comments.
release_notes: Introduce compact preflight orchestration with a fastpath + deep-check staged presubmit, two-stage dependency bootstrap, and a slim presubmit image. Improves average presubmit setup time and reduces network/image costs for frequent PRs. Opt-in flag controls rollout.
notes: Implementation choices: used a declarative .github/preflight.yml so future owners can add rules without code changes; the two-stage bootstrap intentionally pins runtime deps early to maximize cache hits. The lint telemetry emits a small JSON blob to CI analytics to help triage flaky or cold-run problems.
testing_instructions: Local dev: make presubmit-fastpath to run the fast checks; make presubmit-deep to run the full flow. CI: flip .github/feature-flags presubmit.fastpath to enable rollout. Observability: dashboards added under /dashboards/ci-presubmit for tracking setup time and cache hit-rate.
